about: The MotherDuck Dive component catalog. Agents read it to pick components; a Flight that plans pages from components (motherduck-build-malleable-dive) builds its planner rules from the entries that have plan_rule. Order is assembly order.
common_fields: Every block may also carry: caption (one sentence), insight (a 'so what' line, rendered by BlockInsight), about ({ definitions: [{ term, text }], why }, rendered with the source by SourceFooter), probe and hypothesis (a follow-up query an analyst step ran), highlight (x values to emphasise). notes ([{ kind, at, category, note }], added by withNotes and rendered by NotesLine) are what viewers said about a date or value the block shows.

components.label: Stats
components.data: { items: [{ key, label, value, prior?, format, good?, spark?, spark_x?, spark_grain? }], compare? }
components.when: 3-4 headline numbers with their change and a weekly sparkline. The first block on most pages.
components.plan_rule: kpi: 2-4 headline measures from any datasets, with a comparison. Start every page with one (span 12).

components.label: Metric cards
components.when: Headline numbers as separate cards with a change chip, count-up number, context line and sparkline. Inspired by uiarc metric-card.

components.label: Compact stats
components.when: Many small numbers in little space: label, icon indicator, value, trend. Inspired by diceui stat.

components.label: Gauges
components.data: the kpi shape; every item a rate (format pct) or with min/max
components.when: A rate or a value against a target or capacity, with a tick at the comparison. Inspired by diceui gauge.

components.label: Line
components.data: { x: { kind: 'time', grain }, series: [{ key, label, format, good?, muted? }], data: [{ x, [key]: n }], annotations?: [{ x, label, series }], points?: [{ x, series }] }
components.when: A trend over time: 1-3 measures with one unit, or one measure split into up to 6 groups.
components.plan_rule: line: trends over time (a window of 90 days or longer, time_grain week or month). Use series_dimension only to compare a few groups. All measures must share a unit.

components.label: Area
components.when: A trend where the latest value matters: headline value and change, legend toggles, gradient fill, crosshair. Inspired by uiarc line-chart.

components.label: Bar
components.data: { x: { kind: 'category' }, series: [{ key, label, format }, { key: '<key>_prior', muted: true }?], data: [{ x, [key]: n }] }
components.when: Compare a measure across categories, optionally against the previous period. Horizontal when labels are long.
components.plan_rule: bar: compare a measure across a categorical dimension; use a compare to show what changed. All measures must share a unit.

components.label: Table
components.data: the bar shape; a series format 'row' reads _format per row; delta_pct and text columns
components.when: Rankings, exact values, or several measures with different units per row.
components.plan_rule: table: rankings or several measures per row. Never show the same measures by the same dimension as both a bar and a table.

components.label: Drivers
components.data: a table with drivers: true, rows { x: 'dimension: value', before, now, change, share? } and total { label, before, now, format }
components.when: Explains why a measure moved: the values of every other dimension ranked by how much they changed it.
components.plan_rule: drivers: explains why a measure moved: one measure, with the segment as filters; it breaks the change down across every other dimension. Use it when the question asks why, or what drives something.

components.label: Heatmap
components.data: calendar: the line shape with one daily series (or mode 'calendar'); matrix: the line shape with several series (rows) over periods, or { mode: 'matrix', rows, cols, cells: [{ row, col, v }], format }
components.when: Patterns by day (calendar, like an activity heatmap) or a category against time (matrix): weekly rhythms, outliers, when something started. Inspired by uiarc activity-heatmap.
components.plan_rule: heatmap: a measure by day over 90 days or more (dimension empty: a calendar of daily activity), or a measure by a dimension against weeks (dimension set: up to 10 rows). Use it for rhythms and outliers, not for exact values.

components.label: Flow
components.data: { nodes: [{ name, side: 'source'|'target' }], links: [{ source, target, value }], format, source_label, target_label } plus the bar shape of the flows
components.when: How a count flows from one set of categories into another: channel to section, topic to outcome.
components.plan_rule: sankey: how an additive count flows from one dimension (dimension) to another dimension of the same dataset (series_dimension), e.g. channel to section, topic to outcome. Up to 6 values per side.

components.label: Treemap
components.data: { tree: { name, children: [{ name, value } | { name, children }] }, format } or the bar shape with one additive measure
components.when: Part-to-whole for many categories of one additive measure, optionally grouped (click a group to zoom). Inspired by uiarc treemap.
components.plan_rule: treemap: share of one additive measure (count or currency) across up to 20 values of a dimension; set series_dimension to group them into a second level.

components.label: Timeline
components.data: { items: [{ date, title, body?, tone? }], activeIndex? } or a table with timeline: { date, title }
components.when: Events in order: detected shifts, releases, incidents, steps of an investigation. Inspired by diceui timeline.

components.label: Callouts
components.data: { items: [{ tone: critical|warning|positive|info, title, body, block_id?, question?, continuity?: new|ongoing|worsening|improving|resolved, first_seen?, times_seen?, refers_to? }] }
components.when: Findings that need attention. continuity shows how each relates to earlier insights. With a nav prop, items with a question get an Investigate button, and nav.rate/nav.rating add thumbs up and down.

components.label: Form
components.data: { title?, description?, fields: [{ id, kind: text|textarea|select|choice|multi, label, description?, placeholder?, options?: [string | { value, label, description? }], layout?: cards|chips, required? }], submit_label? }
components.when: Questions with an answer: feedback forms, intake, a short survey on a page. nav.submit(blockId, values) receives the answers. The same file has the form-field primitives after shadcn/ui Field (FieldSet, FieldLegend, FieldGroup, Field with orientation vertical|horizontal|responsive and invalid, FieldLabel, FieldContent, FieldTitle, FieldDescription, FieldError, FieldSeparator) and the controls Input, Textarea, Select and ChoiceGroup (radio or checkbox choice cards, or chips). Use them for any input in a Dive.

components.label: Questions
components.data: { items: [{ id, kind: date|topic, x, grain?, dimension?, value?, label, question, options: [string] }] }
components.when: Questions the page asks its viewers about a date or a segment it cannot explain from the data. With nav.annotate and nav.noteFor, each item takes an answer: a category (event, release, campaign, data_issue, expected, noise, other) and a note. The same file has withNotes(block, notes), which pins saved notes to every block that shows that date or value, NotesLine, which renders them under a block, and NoteForm, built from the form fields in kit/field.tsx.

components.label: Date picker
components.data: props: mode 'single'|'range', value (ISO or { from, to }), onChange, min, max, presets
components.when: Let the viewer choose a date or a range. Store the value in useDiveState and use it in SQL.
